title: Cold tire pressure and safety
text: Tire pressure affects safety, durability, and fuel consumption. NHTSA recommends checking tire pressure when tires are cold and using the vehicle manufacturer's recommended pressure from the tire/loading label or owner's manual. A tire can lose pressure after a pothole or curb impact.

title: Low tire pressure warning
text: A tire pressure monitoring system can warn when pressure is significantly underinflated, but drivers should still check tire pressure regularly. Significantly low pressure can increase heat buildup, braking distance, instability, and risk of tire failure.

title: Motorcycle tire inspection
text: Before a ride, inspect motorcycle tire inflation, tread wear, sidewall condition, bulges, embedded objects, wheels, and signs of bearing or seal problems. Check pressure when tires are cold and use the motorcycle manufacturer's specification.

title: Motorcycle brake check
text: Before riding, test the front and rear brake controls individually. Each brake should feel firm and should be able to hold the motorcycle when applied. Inspect brake pads and discs for wear.

title: Throttle and control checks
text: A pre-ride check should include handlebars, levers, cables, hoses, throttle action, mirrors, and switches. The throttle should move freely and return to the closed position when released.

title: Motorcycle fluid and leak checks
text: Inspect engine oil and other specified fluids and look for oil, coolant, brake-fluid, or fuel leaks. Coolant level should be checked according to the manufacturer's procedure and only when the system is safe to inspect.

title: Do not continue driving an overheated engine
text: A coolant-temperature warning can indicate extremely high engine coolant temperature. Hyundai owner's guidance says not to continue driving with an overheated engine because overheating can damage the engine. The exact procedure is vehicle-specific, so the owner's manual should be followed.

title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp
text: A malfunction indicator lamp can illuminate when there is a malfunction in an engine, powertrain, or emissions-related system. Manufacturer guidance recommends inspection when the lamp indicates a fault; the exact meaning depends on the vehicle and fault code.

title: Oil-pressure warning needs prompt attention
text: Low engine-oil pressure can indicate insufficient oil or another fault. Manufacturer guidance warns that continuing to operate the engine after an oil-pressure warning can cause severe damage. The vehicle owner's manual should be followed for the exact warning procedure.

title: Parking brake and brake-system caution
text: Driving with an electronic parking brake applied can overheat the braking system and accelerate wear. If a brake-system warning appears or braking performance is reduced, the vehicle should be inspected and the manufacturer's safety instructions followed.

title: What OBD monitors
text: On-board diagnostics monitors emission-control and some engine-related components. When the system detects a malfunction or deterioration that can affect emissions, it can illuminate the Check Engine or Service Engine Soon light and store diagnostic information.

title: Diagnostic codes guide troubleshooting
text: OBD systems can store diagnostic trouble codes and operating information that help technicians identify a fault. A code narrows the problem area; it does not by itself prove that a particular physical part must be replaced.
source_name: U.S. EPA OBD II Test Procedures

title: Flashing check-engine light is more urgent
text: EPA consumer guidance notes that a flashing dashboard light can indicate a severe engine misfire. In that situation, reducing speed and seeking service promptly is advised because continued severe misfire can damage emissions-control components.

title: Two-wheeler no-start triage
text: For a no-start complaint, first distinguish whether the starter motor turns the engine or the engine does not crank. Useful observations include weak horn or lights, clicking sounds, fuel availability, side-stand/interlock behavior where equipped, and whether the engine cranks normally but fails to fire. These observations narrow the likely system without proving a single fault.

title: Four-wheeler no-start triage
text: For a no-start complaint, identify whether the engine cranks, clicks, or remains silent. Then consider battery/starting system, fuel delivery, ignition, immobilizer/interlock, and sensor-related causes. A symptom alone cannot confirm a failed component.

title: Brake noise and pedal changes
text: Brake squeal, grinding, vibration, pulling, or a changing pedal feel can have different causes, including pad wear, disc/rotor condition, contamination, or hydraulic/system faults. A grinding sound, reduced braking, warning light, or fluid leak should trigger prompt professional inspection rather than a guess at a replacement part.

title: Steering symptoms are safety-sensitive
text: Difficulty steering, new free play, strong pulling, or a sudden change in steering behavior can indicate a safety-critical problem. The app should prioritize stopping in a safe location and arranging inspection rather than suggesting experimentation on public roads.

title: Suspension noises need symptom context
text: Clunks or knocks over bumps may be associated with worn or loose suspension/steering components, but sound alone is insufficient for a diagnosis. Ask when the noise occurs, whether the vehicle pulls, and whether ride height or tire wear has changed.

title: Weak electrical symptoms
text: Slow cranking, repeated clicking, dim lights, or a weak horn can point toward a battery/charging/connection issue, but the battery should be tested before replacement. Corroded or loose terminals can also contribute.

title: Weak cranking symptoms
text: Slow engine cranking, clicking, or dim electrical accessories may indicate a weak battery, poor connection, starter-system issue, or charging problem. Testing the battery and charging system is more reliable than replacing a part based only on the symptom.

title: Mileage complaints require multiple checks
text: A sudden drop in fuel economy can have several causes including tire pressure, driving conditions, maintenance state, drag, and engine/emissions faults. Compare like-for-like driving conditions and check basic maintenance items before assuming a single failed component.
source_name: NHTSA Tire Safety + EPA OBD resources

title: Safety gate for critical symptoms
text: For suspected brake failure, severe overheating, steering-control problems, fuel leaks, heavy smoke, burning electrical smell, or a flashing engine warning combined with severe running problems, prioritize safe stopping and professional inspection. The AI should never present a guess as a confirmed diagnosis.
